# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto, titled "For a Fair Deal," presents a comprehensive vision for transforming British politics and addressing what they describe as years of Conservative neglect across healthcare, the economy, environment, and public services.

## Key Themes

### Economy
The party pledges responsible fiscal management while investing in green infrastructure and renewable energy. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, reforming capital gains tax, increasing the Digital Services Tax on tech giants, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. They commit to fixing the UK-EU trading relationship and supporting small businesses through expanded access to capital.

### Healthcare
The NHS receives significant focus, with promises to guarantee GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Other commitments include guaranteeing NHS dental access for emergency care, placing mental health professionals in every school, boosting cancer survival rates with a 62-day treatment guarantee, and investing in public health to help people live five more healthy years.

### Social Care
The manifesto proposes free personal care based on Scotland's model, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, establishing a Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard minimum wage), and providing statutory respite breaks for unpaid carers. A cross-party commission would develop sustainable long-term funding.

### Environment
Climate commitments include achieving net zero by 2045, generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030, and launching an emergency home insulation programme. The party pledges to tackle the sewage scandal by transforming water companies into public benefit companies, banning executive bonuses until pollution ends, and replacing Ofwat with a stronger regulator.

### Housing
Targets include building 380,000 homes annually (150,000 social homes), banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leaseholds, and ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

### Political Reform
Democratic reforms include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, capping political donations, reforming the House of Lords, and enshrining the Ministerial Code in law.

### International Affairs
The party advocates fixing EU relations through a four-stage roadmap ultimately aiming for Single Market membership, supporting Ukraine, returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, and advocating for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire with a two-state solution.
